html:
SMTO-ART-0010 — SMTO couldn't confirm a saved file is intact

GUID: 2e26e2c3-9ccc-443e-bfde-d26207e3efbf
Slug: artifact-integrity-failed
Domain: ART · Subsystem: art

What happened

  • The stored copy of this file, or a copy being moved between computers, didn't match what SMTO recorded when it saved it. SMTO stopped rather than hand you a file that might be wrong.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Artifacts from this run and find the file. If it has a Download link, try it; if it shows 'Artifact unavailable', SMTO has set that copy aside. A later save may already have worked, so checking first avoids making a duplicate.
  2. If the list shows files still waiting to be collected, select Retry collection once and wait for it to finish. Collection copies the file from its original location again and checks it before keeping it.
  3. If there is still no good copy and Retry collection isn't shown, ask SMTO in a new message to save the file again from where it was made. A fresh save checks the file against the original instead of reusing the bad copy.

What success looks like

  • The file appears in Artifacts from this run and downloads without an error.

If it still fails

  • Check whether the earlier action already happened before trying it again: look in Artifacts from this run first. Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO; repeated failures can mean a disk or network problem. Don't keep retrying, and don't delete the unavailable copy; it helps them find the cause.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Artifact integrity verification failed: stored bytes did not match the recorded size or SHA-256 when opening a stream (the artifact is then quarantined), or Gateway read chunks or a materialization transfer had inconsistent revision, offset, size or digest.

What this means

  • Materialization/streaming observes size/hash or chunk identity inconsistencies, or opening/verifying retained bytes fails and the registry quarantines the artifact. Artifact publication and presentation remain separate from the command that produced a file. Only an explicit pre-dispatch rejection proves that new command did not run; diagnostics do not collect, transfer, quarantine or delete files.

Why this can happen

  • Materialization/streaming observes size/hash or chunk identity inconsistencies, or opening/verifying retained bytes fails and the registry quarantines the artifact.

How to diagnose it

  • Distinguish proven digest mismatch from an underlying read failure wrapped as integrity failure; inspect any original transfer commit.

How to fix it

  • Check the Server log for the diagnostic (stored-blob mismatch with quarantine, or chunk revision/offset mismatch). Compare the blob under versions/ with registered_artifacts size_bytes and sha256 and check disk health; confirm no newer available version exists before re-collecting from the source on the original Gateway, and do not reset a quarantined status by hand.
  • Recollect or retransfer from the authoritative source and verify final size and hash before publication.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect and reconcile authoritative state before repeating a mutation. Do not blindly retry.

How to verify the fix

  • Exact authoritative source bytes and final receipt agree before any supported publication.

What not to do

  • Do not repeat a mutation while the earlier outcome or current owner is unresolved.

Technical notes

  • Artifact publication and presentation remain separate from the command that produced a file. Only an explicit pre-dispatch rejection proves that new command did not run; diagnostics do not collect, transfer, quarantine or delete files.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.

Do not confuse with / related errors

  • SMTO-EXE-0004 — Execution outcome is unknown
